institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing specific, I wasn't planning on going on exchange in the first place but then I changed my mind.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Okay. A bit confusing. I was lucky that I was going on exchange with some of my friends from home. So in that way I think it was easier than if I had been on my own.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive assistance when I arrived

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really not easy to find affordable housing. I dont think there even was on campus housing. Paris is a pretty expensive city for housing but I guess if you have a big budget, it would be much more easy. A tip is finding housing close to or outside the periphery but I wouldnt recommend as it kind of ruins the point of living the 'Parisian life'.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a basic recommendation, but I would avoid the areas that are filled with tourists, arrondissements 1,2,4, especially. I can really recommend the 9th, 17th and 18th which are still crowded but much more affordable and lowkey.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was really unorganised and very much first come, first served. We had 24 hours to register for courses - some mandatory from home and some where we could choose whatever. All courses were filled in the first 3 minutes. The point is that people are registering and unregistering thorughout the day and so some courses could be open again though they had first been filled. Still, this did not really happen. I only got 1/5 courses that I meant to have.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email and physical at the administration office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only got one I initially wanted. So not really successful. A lot of exchange students had this problem and it seemed like it was the same problem for the university every semester. I also think that my home university should take more responsibility in ensuring that the host university actually have a registering process that makes sense for the students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very stressful so be prepared for that. And there is really no help to get before arriving. They dont really answer on email until the semester starts and their administration office also closed for a week after we arrived. But also know that this is a general problem and there is almost always some kind of solution

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was not so difficult, but really really time consuming !!! I have always studied a lot during the semester but I didn't even have time to read out syllabus as we had so many assignments and presentations. It reminded me of high school in Denmark. A lot of homework and assignments. Also, they are also really really strict about attending.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Oral presentations, assignments such as essays etc... much like Danish highschool. Also be prepared for some classes were it is only presentations that day.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EU Challenges and Opportunities 
Comparative Politics
Comparative Social Policy in Europe
Ethics of War and Peace
Religion, politics and society

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Religion, politics and society was really interesting. And Comparative Social Policy in Europe was also really surprising. It is kind of a heavy course in terms of information and theory but really important knowledge and usable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Public transport was much more expensive than I expected. I know that some other students leased bikes throughout their exchange, much like Swpfiets in Denmark. It was also possible to buy a monthly payed card for the train but I thought it was pretty expensive. Still, I would recommend buying something like those because it ends up being more expensive not doing it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport and grocery shopping were more expensive. I think the price range is pretty much the same as in Denmark. But lunch in general was less expensive, both at my university and at cafes, you could buy decent sandwiches, salads etc for maybe 5 euros.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sciences Po offered lots of cultural, athletic and social activities. Most of them were organised by students but some of them were also done by professors. I know that one of my professors had a weekly film club for all where there were debates and so on. All for free. Other than that I know there were yoga classes and Im sure lots of social clubs if you looked into it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend exploring the city by walking around without a plan. Still, go to see the typical Parisian things like the Eiffel Tower, explore the Louvre Museum without trying to rush it, wander through Montmartre and visit Sacré-Cœur, and spend time walking along the Seine River, especially in the evening. It may be mainstream but incredibly beautifiul.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to see the Versailles Palace and take a walk in the garden. Just take trips outside of Paris. With the TGV you can go and visit all aorund France, go to Lille or Marseille just to experience other places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Paris is an international city, so it’s quite used to foreign students, which makes adapting feel natural. Daily routines, university life, and social environments are easy to get into, even if you don’t speak perfect French.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I don’t have specific tips, but being open, attending classes regularly, and spending time in shared spaces like cafés or campus areas helps create opportunities to meet people naturally.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn’t experience any major cultural differences that were particularly challenging. Most differences were small, such as communication styles or social norms, and were easy to get used to over time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I most appreciated the strong focus on enjoying everyday life, especially through food, cafés, and socializing. The culture encourages taking time to relax, meet friends, and enjoy meals rather than rushing. I also really valued the emphasis on art, history, and aesthetics, which is visible everywhere in the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared before the course registration
2. Look into what the requirements are for the courses - the courses can vary a lot in terms of assignments, exams, syllabus etc.
3. That everything will work out!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking advantage of how much Paris and its surroundings have to offer by exploring both the city itself and nearby destinations. And also, even basic French can be helpful in everyday situations and is appreciated by locals, so making an effort to learn a few phrases goes a long way.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was living in the environment of Paris. Being surrounded by history, culture, and beautiful buildings made everyday life feel special

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was that the courses were very time consuming.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
